Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: issue #9910 (CI triage for PR #9899, branch `ai/issue-9887`)

Planning ref: `ai/issue-9887` at `f6ef4b5126f985332322502ff34da33b97d27988`. Integration branch mismatch: false.

The clarify phase found the issue clear, and its auto-posted `/answer` adds no constraints.

## Files likely to change

- `docs/INVENTORY.md`

## Acceptance

ACCEPTANCE: test tests/inventory_parity.py red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_gh_call_counter.py
ACCEPTANCE: check tests-release-and-log-analysis
ACCEPTANCE: check lint
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: this adds two inventory lines on a PR feature branch; the PR's own CI covers it and no post-merge workflow depends on the change.

## Functions or modules to implement

No code changes. Add two entries to the `## Scripts` section of `docs/INVENTORY.md`, right after the `scripts/gh_api_retry.py` line (line 220) and before the `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` line (line 221):

- `` - `scripts/gh_call_counter/gh` — `gh` PATH shim that logs one allowlisted-subcommand/paginate/token-kind line per GitHub CLI call (never arguments or values) and then execs the next `gh` on PATH unchanged; installed by `gh_call_counter_install` in gh_helpers.sh (issue #9887). ``
- `` - `scripts/gh_call_counter/gh-call-counter-summary` — Summarises the `gh_call_counter` shim log into the `calls_in_job=` / `paginated_in_job=` / `calls_by_token=` keys of the `GH_PAT_BUDGET phase=end` line. ``

Why there:
- Byte-wise, `gh_api_retry.py` < `gh_call_counter/...` < `gh_helpers.sh`, because `a` < `c` < `h` after `gh_`. Within the pair, `gh` sorts before `gh-call-counter-summary`.
- The wording comes from the PR's own descriptions: README.md lines 615–617 and `agents.d/9887-gh-call-counter.md` lines 8–9.
- Each line must use the exact `` - `path` — role `` shape with an em dash, which `tests/inventory_parity.py` checks around lines 200–203. Any other separator fails with `expected '- \`path\` — role'`.

## Data structures affected

Only the `docs/INVENTORY.md` `## Scripts` list. No schemas, environment variables or identifiers change.

## API or interface changes

None.

## Decisions

### D1 — Register the scripts in the inventory instead of exempting them
- Chosen: add two `## Scripts` entries to `docs/INVENTORY.md`.
- Alternatives considered: list the paths in `tests/inventory_exemptions.txt`; remove the README.md and agents references; loosen `tests/inventory_parity.py`.
- Why: the issue forbids weakening the parity gate or deleting the references. These are tracked, executable support scripts that docs cite, so they belong in the inventory. An exemption would hide them.

### D2 — Leave the `tests/test_gh_call_counter.py` pre-push note alone
- Chosen: change nothing for that test.
- Alternatives considered: re-embed the shim or the summary into `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`, or change file modes.
- Why: on this ref the two heredocs in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` (`GH_CALL_COUNTER_SHIM` and `GH_CALL_COUNTER_SUMMARY`) are byte-identical to the canonical files. I checked this with the test's own `_embedded()` extraction logic. Both files are tracked as mode `100755`. Nothing about embedding or executable bits needs fixing. CI's pytest catch-all collects the file (`tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`), so CI will show any remaining behavioural failure.

### D3 — No changelog fragment
- Chosen: none.
- Alternatives considered: add `changelog.d/9910-*.md`.
- Why: this is a docs registry fix inside PR #9899's own change. That PR carries its own changelog fragment (`changelog.d/9887-gh-call-counter.md`), and no user-facing behaviour changes.

## Security considerations

- No trust boundary, endpoint, secret, token handling or external input is touched. The change is a two-line edit to a markdown file.
- The new role text names no token values, secrets or credentials. It only names the token kinds `pat`, `github_token` and `other`, which the PR's own docs already publish.
- Abuse cases: none apply. The inventory is documentation that a test reads.
- Money handling: not applicable.

## Potential risks or edge cases

- **Wrong separator or bullet shape.** The parity parser stops with a `FAIL` line if an entry is not in `` - `path` — role `` form. Copy the em dash from a neighbouring line.
- **Conflict found locally, snapshot only.** Run on the planning snapshot, `tests/inventory_parity.py` also reports `.github/workflows/propagate-consumer-secrets.yml` as "unexpected", both in INVENTORY and in its references at README.md:4854 and agents.md:6370. The snapshot filter dropped that workflow because of its credential-like name, so it is absent locally and in `isolated-base`. CI run 44952622917 does not report it, so it is an artefact of the snapshot, not a real failure. Do not edit anything about it.
- **Conflict: line number.** The issue cites `agents.md:2296`, but line 2296 of the working-tree `agents.md` is unrelated text. The parity tool reports the reference against `agents.md`, but it comes from the pending fragment `agents.d/9887-gh-call-counter.md`, which the tool appears to read in assembled form. This changes nothing in the fix.
- **Overlapping PRs.** Open PRs #9359 and #9510 also touch `docs/INVENTORY.md`. Adding two lines in the middle of the alphabetical list keeps the merge-conflict risk small.

## Testing considerations

- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/inventory_parity.py`. Today it reports the two missing `gh_call_counter` script entries and three undocumented-path references (README.md:616 once, agents.md:2296 twice). After the change those five must be gone. In the local snapshot only the `propagate-consumer-secrets.yml` lines remain, for the reason in the risks section; in CI it must print `OK: inventory parity validated ...`.
- `tests/test_ci_inventory_parity_order_contract.py` (ci.yml line 2826) runs alongside it unchanged. It checks the order of CI steps, not inventory lines.
- In CI, `tests/test_gh_call_counter.py` runs under pytest. pytest is not installed in this sandbox, so only the parity and executable-bit checks were confirmed locally, by hand. The pass-through tests are left to CI.
- No new test files.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends docs/INVENTORY.md
Scope-mode justification: The failing gate is the existing inventory-parity contract, and the issue's own root cause and suggested fix both point to two missing entries in `docs/INVENTORY.md`. Following §6 Core Priorities in `unattended_system_instructions.md` (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete fix is exactly those two lines, so there is nothing to choose between a shortcut and a complete option. Changing `tests/inventory_parity.py`, the exemptions file, or the README.md and agents references would weaken the contract or break the issue's explicit constraints. A check of `tests/test_gh_call_counter.py` found nothing to fix on this ref (embedding matches and files are executable), so widening scope to it is not justified.
